bib.title: Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Overview (Chapter 1: Introduction)

question: What is the formal framework of sequential decision making (agent, environment, MDP/POMDP and variants) and how do RL methods, exploration and reward design fit into it?
contributions: A unified agent-environment model with explicit internal state, predict/update, encoder/decoder and learning algorithm (Fig 1.2)
A taxonomy of canonical models (POMDP, MDP, goal-conditioned, contextual MDP, contextual bandit, belief-state MDP, optimisation as decision problem)
A high-level map of value-based, policy-based and model-based RL (Table 1.1)
Short treatments of partial observability, exploration, reward design and experimental practice

results.claim: With gamma=0.99, reaching a terminal reward of 1.0 in 15 steps yields about 0.86 discounted reward.
results.quote: if γ = 0.99, then an agent that reaches a terminal reward of 1.0 in 15 steps will receive an expected discounted reward of 0.9915 = 0.86, whereas if it takes 17 steps it will only get 0.9917 = 0.84.
results.note: Exponents 15 and 17 are flattened in the text layer (0.99^15).

results.claim: Discount gamma = 1 - 1/T implies an expected lifetime of order T steps; gamma=0.95 corresponds to 2 seconds at 0.1 s per step.
results.quote: if each step is 0.1 seconds, then γ = 0.95 corresponds to 2 seconds.

results.claim: Epsilon-greedy with epsilon=0.1 gives action probabilities 0.05/0.95 whenever the two reward estimates differ, while Boltzmann (tau=1) varies smoothly with the estimates.
results.baseline_value: 0.88 (Boltzmann, R-hat 4.00 vs 6.00 in state s2 row)
results.setup: Simple MDP with 6 states and 2 actions, epsilon=0.1, tau=1
results.quote: Comparison of ϵ-greedy policy (with ϵ = 0.1) and Boltzmann policy (with τ = 1) for a simple MDP with 6 states and 2 actions.
results.table: Table 1.2, rows R-hat(s,a1)=4.00,R-hat(s,a2)=6.00, columns pi_eps and pi_tau
results.note: Table text layer is column-flattened; row/column mapping read from order, check the page image before citing.

results.claim: Epsilon-greedy explores every action with probability at least epsilon/|A|, so it is suboptimal unless epsilon is annealed to 0.
results.quote: Unfortunately, this heuristic can be shown to be suboptimal, since it explores every action with at least a constant probability ϵ/|A|, although this can be solved by annealing ϵ to 0 over time.

results.claim: Policy gradient provably converges to a local optimum for many policy classes, while Q-learning may diverge with function approximation; the score-function estimator has high variance.
results.quote: Policy gradient methods have the advantage that they provably converge to a local optimum for many common policy classes, whereas Q-learning may diverge when approximation is used (Section 2.5.2.5).

results.claim: Potential-based shaping F=gamma*Phi(s')-Phi(s) leaves the optimal policy unchanged (shaped return = original plus a constant).
In the tabular case potential-based shaping is equivalent to initialising V(s)=Phi(s).
results.quote: they prove that (in the tabular case) this approach is equivalent to initializing the value function to V (s) = Φ(s)

results.claim: MineCLIP reward model scores the last K frames against a language goal, trained contrastively on video-text pairs; figure shows correlation 0.95.
results.setup: Minecraft in MineDojo; reward R(o(t-K:t), g)
results.note: 0.95 appears only as a figure label; its meaning is not explained in the chapter text.

results.claim: Agarwal et al. recommend the interquartile mean (mean of samples between the 0.25 and 0.75 percentiles) with bootstrap or Gaussian uncertainty when aggregating across environments.
results.setup: Reporting across environments such as Atari games
results.quote: the interquartile mean (IQM) of the performance metric, which is the mean of the samples between the 0.25 and 0.75 percentiles

limits: Introductory survey chapter: no experiments of its own; all numbers are worked examples or quoted.
Optimal POMDP solution is stated to be wildly intractable [PT87; KLC98].
RNN policies do not plan information-gathering actions (no explicit belief state).
Frame stacking cannot capture long-range dependencies.
Section references point to later chapters not in this PDF (2-7); detail on TD, DQN, PPO, bandit regret, LLM RL lives there.
practices: Build on existing RL software rather than from scratch because RL losses are unstable (Sec 1.3.7, Table 1.3).
Report interquartile mean across environments with bootstrap or Gaussian uncertainty; RL experiments are high variance (Sec 1.3.7).
Use a recurrent/stateful policy or frame stacking for partial observability; belief-state solution is intractable (Sec 1.3.4).
Anneal epsilon to 0 or use Boltzmann/epsilon-z-greedy to fix epsilon-greedy suboptimality and dithering (Sec 1.3.5).
Use potential-based reward shaping to keep the optimal policy (Sec 1.3.6.5).
Add policy-gradient baselines (V or advantage, i.e. actor-critic) to cut variance (Sec 1.3.2).

terms.definition: Environment with hidden world state w_t, noisy/partial observation o_t; agent keeps internal belief state z_t
Special case of a POMDP in which the environment states are observed, w_t = o_t = s_t
G_t = r_t + gamma r_{t+1} + ... ; G_t = r_t + gamma G_{t+1}
V_pi(s_t) = E[G_t | pi], the expected reward-to-go
Reward R(s,a|g) = I(s = g), or dense sim(s,g); policy pi(a|s,g) is a universal policy
MDP whose dynamics and rewards depend on a hidden static context
POMDP where p(w_t|w_{t-1},a_t)=p(w_t); the agent does not affect the state, only the rewards
MDP whose state is the posterior b_t = p(w|h_t), updated by Bayes rule; solving it solves exploration-exploitation
Bandit variant that maximises the final reward of the estimated best arm after T trials
Simple regret is the regret at the last step; cumulative regret L_T = E[sum l_t]
Model trained to directly predict future observations p(o_{t+1}|h_t,a_t) without explicit latent state
Random action w.p. epsilon; or pi_tau(a|s) proportional to exp(R-hat/tau)
Misspecified reward is maximised but not what the user desired (paperclip maximizer)
R(s,a)=0 for almost all states and actions, requiring deep exploration
Policy gradient with learned V_w or advantage A_w as baseline; actor = pi_theta, critic = V_w or A_w
